paper.title: Experimental evidence of an upper limit for hydrogen storage at 77 K on activated carbons

defaults.verified_by: Agent B (sonnet, independent re-extraction of Tables 1-2): Table 1 texture 0 mismatches (9 samples x 6 params), all Table 2 uptake cells 0 mismatches; the 4 n.d. cells correctly handled; the 298 K/20 MPa 1.1 wt% across-samples maximum correctly excluded. uptake_type=excess confirmed. Agent C adjudications: (1) pressure_bar unit fix -- the paper states MPa, so 5 MPa->50 bar (298 K) and 4 MPa->40 bar (77 K) (Agent B caught the un-converted magnitudes); (2) pore_diameter_method DR_characteristic_energy->stoeckli_L0 (the paper uses Stoeckli's exact L0=10.8/(E0-11.4), cited to Stoeckli); (3) multi-device modelling -- collapsed to ONE excess row per (sample, T, P) (18 rows, not 32) so the corpus's one-point-per-sample/T/P plotting invariant holds; the parallel lab/method values (IJL/ICMPE volumetric at 298 K; ICMPE volumetric/ICB gravimetric at 77 K) are in each row's source_location. He void-volume (ICMPE) + experimental buoyancy (ICB) corrections -> calibration point -> all rows Tier A.

notes.type: uptake_type=excess (exact-word rule): Table 2 is 'Hydrogen uptake (excess)' and the text reports 'H2 excess capacities' throughout
notes.multidev: Table 2 reports each sample measured by up to three independent labs/devices (IJL volumetric and ICMPE volumetric at 298 K/5 MPa; ICMPE volumetric and ICB gravimetric at 77 K/4 MPa) to demonstrate reproducibility. The corpus holds ONE excess row per (sample, T, P): recording each device as its own row would double-count every material in the Chahine / uptake-vs-area statistics (tests/test_plotting.py pins one point per sample/T/P). So the ICMPE value is recorded (it is reported for every sample at both temperatures) and source_location gives the parallel lab/method value(s), which agree within the stated +-0.1 wt% -- the paper's central claim. Where ICMPE is n.d. at 298 K the IJL volumetric value is recorded instead. measurement_method is volumetric_sieverts (the recorded ICMPE/IJL value); the ICB gravimetric cross-check is in source_location.
notes.method: three devices: IJL lab-made volumetric (298 K, to 20 MPa, Hemmes EoS, vessel-compression corrected); ICMPE volumetric PCI Sieverts (77 & 298 K, to 8 MPa, GASPAK EoS, He void correction, dry mass); ICB VTI gravimetric (77 K, to 8 MPa, experimental buoyancy correction). H2 purity >5N (IJL) / 6N (ICMPE). The He void-volume and buoyancy corrections -> calibration point by hand (tiering doc l.24)
notes.sa: surface_area_method=BET (high-resolution N2 at 77 K, P/P0 to 1e-7); total pore volume V0.99 (Gurvitch single-point at P/P0=0.99); micropore_volume = VDR,N2 (DR on N2); micropore_volume_co2 = VDR,CO2 (DR on CO2 at 273 K, pores <0.7 nm); pore_volume_method=DR (describes the DR micropore volumes), probe N2
notes.l0: average_pore_diameter = L0, the average pore width computed by the Stoeckli-Ballerini relation L0=10.8/(E0-11.4) (E0 the DR characteristic energy), cited to Stoeckli (ref 33); pore_diameter_method=stoeckli_L0 -- the paper uses Stoeckli's L0 formula explicitly, which the manual recognises as a category distinct from HYC-0024's 'DR characteristic-energy slit width' (Agent B HYC-0047 adjudication)
notes.rho: skeletal_density = qHe, the true density by He pycnometry (Table 1)
notes.excl: the 298 K / 20 MPa maximum excess of 1.1 wt% (conclusions) is a single across-samples maximum, not a per-sample tabulated value, and is not recorded; CO2 uptake (VDR,CO2) is a texture probe, not H2
notes.chahine: 77 K, 4 MPa excess; the paper's own finding is an upper limit of 6.4 wt% at ~2630 m2/g (close to the 6.8 wt% theoretical), so the high 77 K values are physically bounded (no physics override)

S1.label: M1149
S1.material_description: activated carbon from NaOH/KOH chemical activation of Moszczenica (Polish) anthracite; labelled by BET area 1149.0 m2/g
S1.activation_method: chemical activation with NaOH or KOH (XOH/anthracite 1-3), 973-1073 K 1 h under N2; washed with 1 M HCl then water
S1.purification_method: washed with 1 M HCl then distilled water until pH ~6
